report:
MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS



> Spur formation and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage, reflecting osteoarthritis of left knee 
  Tiny subchondral cysts in femoral trochlea; small cystic change over tibial intercondylar eminance.
  Focal wearing articular cartilage of medial patella, reflecting grade 2-3 chondromalacia.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with suspicious of extending into the surface, R/O tear.
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis. SMall Baker's cyst
> Varicose veins, more prominent at medial side.
Increased fat stranding along the pes anserinus, in favor of paratendinitis.

Impression: 
1. C/W osteoarthritis of left knee, with grade 3-4 chondromalacia of patellofemoral joint.
2. Degeneration and R/O tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. Paratendinitis of pes anserinus.
4. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
5. Small Baker's cyst with perifocal edema over medial popliteal fossa.
6. Varicose veins.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Lateral menisküs anterior posterior hornu ve gövde kesimde grade II dejenerasyon, serbest kenarda horizontal yırtık izlenmektedir. Arka çapraz bağ, lateral ve medial kollateral ligaman normaldir.Anterior çapraz bağda miksoid dejenerasyona sekonder sinyal değişikliği izlenmiştir. Distal kuadriseps normaldir. MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

> The contour of ACL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of tear.
> Slight increased signal intensity of PCL on T1WI and F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
 > Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial and lateral plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
 > Ill-defined bone marrow edema in posterior aspect of tibial plateau with slight depressed contour, in favor of bone contusion with R/O occult subchondral fracture.
> There are linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus and lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, R/O degeneration.
> Heterogenous signal intensity of articular cartilage and focal thin cartilage at odd facet, in favor of grade 2-3 patellar chondromalacia.
> Mild fat stranding along medial collateral ligament, R/O grade 1 injury.
> Spur formation of knee joint
> Increased fat stranding of between pes anserinus near the tibial insertion and mild increased intensity inside, R/O grade 1-2 strain.
> Muscle edema at popliteus muscle and plantaris muscle and soleus muscle and increase intermuscular fat stranding, most due to trauma.

Impression: 
1. Tear of anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Bone contusion in posterior asepct of tibial plateau; the possibility of occult subchondral fracture can't excluded.
3. R/O grade 1-2 strain of pes anserinus and grade 1 MCL injury.
4. In favor of degeneration of meniscus.
5. Massive joint effusion
6. Degeneration of knee joint and grade 2-3 patellar chondromalacia.
7. Muscle strain at posterior aspect of proximal leg and subcutaneous edema around knee.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Findings: There is a moderately large knee effusion. No evidence of synovitis. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL and LCL. Moderate - severe thickening of the proximal half of MCL is noted in keeping with a grade II MCL sprain.  There is a 10 x 18 mm focus of articular cartilage loss in the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle but no underlying bony change. Normal tibial articular cartilage. Normal lateral tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: Moderately large knee effusion. Grade II MCL sprain with persistent thickening. Focal articular cartilage defect in the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

MRI RIGHT KNEE

INDICATION: Persistent right knee pain for several years, with seen in pt, had improvement, recent flare 1-2 weeks ago, no changes, no trauma, nothing seen on prior imaging

Routine MRI of the right knee shows no medial or lateral meniscal tear. ACL and PCL are intact. Extensor mechanism intact. Collateral ligaments intact.

No joint effusion. No Baker's cyst. No fluid collections. Full-thickness cartilage fissures are seen along the medial patella with significant underlying bone marrow edema measuring 15 mm transverse by 10 mm in depth by 10 mm in length, along the medial patella. No findings to suggest previous patellar dislocation, for clinical correlation. 

Edema is seen within the superior aspect of Hoffa's fat pad, just inferior to the lateral patella. There is a 3 mm bright PD focus just inferior to the patella which may represent a small focus of fat or bony fragment. TT TG is normal.

IMPRESSION:

No internal derangement.

Severe chondromalacia patella with cartilage fissures and intense bony edema in the medial half of the patella.

Edema in the superior aspect of Hoffa's fat pad, inferior to the lateral patella where there is a 3 mm globule of fat or possible bony fragment [could be evaluated by x-ray]. Findings suggest Hoffitis/fat pad impingement process.
